sources.what: Pascal, Pensées: Brunschvicg 425 ('All men seek happiness') and 430 (the two natures: 'none other has known that man is the most excellent creature')
sources.translator: C. Kegan Paul (1828-1902), The Thoughts of Blaise Pascal, from Molinier's text, 1885 (Bohn 1888)
sources.note: Kegan Paul uses Molinier's arrangement, not Brunschvicg's: locate B425 and B430 by their opening words and give Brunschvicg numbers in the ref. Trotter (Gutenberg #18269) was not used: his death date is uncertain (see journeys-notes).
Do not use unless Trotter's death before 1955 is confirmed. The Gutenberg #18269 file is the 1958 Dutton printing with Eliot's introduction (in copyright).

sources.what: Chesterton, Orthodoxy (1908), ch. VI 'The Paradoxes of Christianity'
sources.note: Same Gutenberg file as After the death of God (which reads ch. II and IX).

sources.what: Jordan Peterson, The Psychological Significance of the Biblical Stories (YouTube lecture series, May-Dec 2017), lectures on Cain and Abel and on Jacob; We Who Wrestle with God (2024); Tom Holland, Dominion (2019); Ayaan Hirsi Ali, 'Why I am now a Christian', UnHerd, 11 November 2023; Paul Kingsnorth, Against the Machine (2025), and his essays on becoming Orthodox (First Things, 'The Cross and the Machine', 2021); Iain McGilchrist, The Master and His Emissary (2009), The Matter with Things (2021); Christopher Kaczor and Matthew Petrusek, Jordan Peterson, God, and Christianity (2021); Justin Brierley, The Surprising Rebirth of Belief in God (2023); Bible Society, The Quiet Revival (2025)
sources.note: In copyright: our own words, at most one short quotation (under 25 words). All living: cite exactly where each said it, represent fairly, never imply endorsement. Statistics: cite The Quiet Revival with its date and the YouGov method, and its published critics.

art.why: No NGA painting of Jacob wrestling the angel (searched titles and descriptions for wrestl, jacob).
No NGA Christ before Pilate or Ecce Homo (searched pilate, ecce homo, christ before). Correa's flagellation scene is claimed by Dostoevsky.

art.title: A View of the Mountain Pass Called the Notch of the White Mountains (Crawford Notch)
art.why: Wild mountain country with storm clouds, broken stumps and a lone rider on the new road: wilderness and the coming of the machine, Kingsnorth's theme (describe only what the NGA text says).

art.title: Harvest Scene in the Delaware Valley
art.why: A wide field with workers, a ray of light breaking through the clouds onto it: the field of Matthew 13:44. No NGA painting of a treasure or pearl of that parable.

music.why: Orthodox vigil, the worship Kingsnorth joined.
